title: Can Legal AI Know When It Is Wrong? And Do Students Know When It Is?
abstract: arXiv:2608.21089v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into the Indian judiciary promises access to justice but introduces severe risks. We identify the 'inertia of confidence'--an overconfidence phenomenon analogous to the Dunning-Kruger effect where LLMs provide incorrect legal verdicts with near-maximum confidence, driven by a hypothesized 'precedent overfitting' bias. Phase I of our socio-technical audit tested ChatGPT (GPT-5.2), Meta AI, and Perplexity AI on a 60-case battery regarding the Indian Contract Act, 1872, and the shift toward statutory enforcement of specific performance. We introduce the High-Confidence Error Rate (HCER) to quantify incorrect verdicts delivered with dangerous certainty (>= 9 on a 1-10 scale). All models struggled with statutory updates. Meta AI proved most vulnerable (31.7% HCER), frequently misapplying pre-amendment rules with a 9.1/10 mean confidence, followed by Perplexity (15.0%) and ChatGPT (6.7%).   Phase II inv

translated_title: 法律人工智能能知道自己错了吗？学生能知道吗？
translated_abstract: 摘要：将大型语言模型（LLMs）整合到印度司法系统中，有望实现司法公正，但同时也引入了严重风险。我们识别出“信心惯性”——一种类似于邓宁-克鲁格效应的过度自信现象，即LLMs以接近最大置信度提供错误的法律判决，这由假设的“先例过拟合”偏差驱动。我们社会技术审计的第一阶段测试了ChatGPT（GPT-5.2）、Meta AI和Perplexity AI，使用60个案例的测试集，涉及1872年《印度合同法》及向具体履行法定执行的转变。我们引入了高置信错误率（HCER）来量化以危险确定性（1-10分制中≥9分）提供的错误判决。所有模型在法定更新方面均表现不佳。Meta AI最为脆弱（HCER为31.7%），经常以9.1/10的平均置信度错误应用修订前规则，其次是Perplexity（15.0%）和ChatGPT（6.7%）。第二阶段邀请...
tldr: 该论文通过引入“信心惯性”和高置信错误率（HCER）概念，揭示了法律大型语言模型在印度司法应用中会以极高置信度输出错误判决的风险，并评估了不同模型的脆弱性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the "inertia of confidence" and the High-Confidence Error Rate (HCER) to reveal that legal LLMs can output incorrect verdicts with dangerously high confidence in Indian judicial applications, assessing the vulnerability of different models.
